question: Can the source-native single-visit effectiveness E_k be matched to the same invasive-ant disturbed/undisturbed context used for visitor-specific visit rates V_k?

source_method_readout.quantity_component_QNC: Pollinator observations; visits were explicitly classified as ant-disturbed (>6 ants/30 min) versus undisturbed for the invasive-ant analysis.
source_method_readout.quality_component_QLC: Fruit and seed set resulting from single visits by each pollinator visitor class.
source_method_readout.article_level_result: Ant presence was associated with lower pollinator visitation in Polyscias crassa and Syzygium wrightii; the source does not state that single-visit QLC was estimated separately within disturbed versus undisturbed ant contexts.

reason: A pooled/source-wide visitor-specific QLC cannot be transported into disturbed and undisturbed context units merely because QNC and QLC coexist in the same study. The frozen mapping contract requires matched population/context hierarchy for rate-weighted effective service.
reopen_rule: Reopen only if raw/source-native metadata explicitly link each single-visit effectiveness observation to the ant disturbed/undisturbed context used for QNC, or a prospective study measures V_k and E_k in the same repeated context units.
claim_boundary: This does not weaken the Seychelles ecological propagation result or its direct pollinator-effectiveness evidence. It only blocks the narrower empirical mapping of ant-driven network context to rate-weighted effective service.
